picked.t: Vietnamese workers spend 4.5 months of wages to secure jobs abroad
picked.body: Costs have fallen 23.8% from VND164.9 million ($6,340) in 2021, according to analysis released Sept. 8 by the National Statistics Office with technical support from the International Organization for Migration. Average first-month income abroad rose 25.4% over the same period, from VND22.4 million ($860) to VND28.1 million ($1,080). Nguyen Thi Ngoc Lan of the office's Population and Labor Statistics Division said a first month's wage abroad runs 3.3 times the average income of a worker at home, which is VND8.5 million ($327). Payments to recruitment companies and individual brokers take 52.8% of what a worker spends, an average of VND94.5 million ($3,635) among those who paid them. Training and document preparation account for 33.7%, travel 11.1% and other expenses 2.3%. Three markets: Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, which together take 76.7% of Vietnamese workers going abroad, carry the highest costs. Workers heading to Japan paid an average of VND140.8 million ($5,415) in 2025, those going to South Korea VND139.4 million ($5,360) and those to Taiwan VND130.2 million ($5,010). Other destinations averaged nearly VND86 million ($3,310). Lan said costs climb as education levels fall, with one group paying as much as VND155.6 million ($5,985). By skill level, medium-skilled workers paid around VND143 million ($5,500), low-skilled workers VND109 million ($4,190) and high-skilled workers just under VND68 million ($2,615). Workers typically spend about six months preparing before departure, and around seven months for those bound for Japan and South Korea. Some 53.9% of those surveyed borrowed to cover the fees. The statistics office cautioned that this part of the study, which drew on 3,596 migrant workers across six provinces and cities, used non-probability sampling and does not represent all Vietnamese workers abroad. Elementary occupations account for 33% of Vietnamese working abroad, craft and related trades about 24%, and machine and equipment operation 16%. Workers with a college diploma or higher earn an average of VND42.6 million ($1,640) in their first month, those with elementary or intermediate vocational training VND27.6 million ($1,060), high school graduates VND26 million ($1,000) and lower secondary graduates about VND22 million ($845). Costs have fallen from previous years but remain high, Lan said, given that most workers going abroad come from rural areas and more than half must borrow. She said regulators need to keep pushing costs down, make fees transparent and control informal charges, while raising workers' skill levels and helping them find work when they return. Nguyen Hai Ly, deputy head of the legal affairs division at the Department of Overseas Labor under the Ministry of Home Affairs, said recruitment and brokerage fees still make up a large share of what workers pay, with most of the excess arising from informal intermediaries who operate before a worker reaches a licensed company. He credited the decline in costs to the 2020 Law on Vietnamese Guest Workers. It abolished brokerage fees charged to workers and shifted them onto companies, and capped service fees at one month's salary for each year of a contract. An amendment to that law, passed by the National Assembly on Aug. 24 and taking effect March 1, 2027, further tightens the ceiling on charges collected outside service fees and stiffens penalties for companies that break the rules. It also caps the wait between selection and departure at 180 days, obliging companies that miss the deadline to compensate workers and refund what they paid. The Department of Overseas Labor said it will use bilateral negotiations to push foreign partners and employers to share recruitment costs, airfares and training, moving step by step toward a model in which workers pay no recruitment fees at all. Data on returning workers will also be integrated into the employment services system to connect them with employers, particularly foreign-invested firms from the markets where those workers were previously posted.

picked.t: ‘아시아 최고’ 푸꾸옥, 외국인 여행객 급증에 관광수입 ‘짭짤’…8월 기준 41.7조 동 전년동기比 47.5%↑
picked.body: 베트남 푸꾸옥의 사오비치. (사진=SG) 아시아에서 가장 아름다운 섬으로 꼽히는 베트남 푸꾸옥이 올 들어 국내외 방문객 급증에 관광 수입도 큰 폭의 증가세를 보이고 있다. 안장성(An Giang) 관광국에 따르면, 8월 기준 푸꾸옥의 관광 수입은 41조7,000억 동(약 15억9,880만 달러)에 달한 것으로 잠정 집계됐다. 이는 전년 동기 대비 47.5% 급증한 수준으로, 특히 증가한 외국인 관광객이 시장 성장을 견인했다. 8월 기준 푸꾸옥을 방문한 외국인 관광객 수는 170만 명으로, 연간 목표치의 85%를 달성했다. 8월 한 달만 놓고 보면 관광 수입은 5조2,600억 동(약 2억170만 달러)으로 전년 동월 대비 54.3% 늘었는데, 이 기간 외국인 관광객은 94% 급증한 21만2,000명을 기록했다. 앞서 푸꾸옥은 지난 한 해 44조 동(약 16억8,700만 달러)의 관광 수입을 올린 바 있다. 일반적으로 푸꾸옥의 관광 성수기는 매년 11월부터 이듬해 4월까지 건기로, 이 시기는 맑은 날씨와 잔잔한 바다, 낮은 습도가 특징이다. 앞서 푸꾸옥은 지난해 콘데나스트트래블러(Condé Nast Traveler) 독자들이 꼽은 ‘아시아에서 가장 아름다운 섬’ 1위(세계 3위)로 선정돼 화제를 모으기도 했다. 이러한 가운데 베트남 정치국은 지난달 국가관광개발에 관한 결의안을 통해 푸꾸옥을 국제적 경쟁력을 갖추고 대형 국제행사도 유치할 수 있는 고급 해변리조트이자 새로운 성장 거점으로 육성한다는 비전을 제시한 바 있어, 지역 관광 산업 성장세는 한동안 계속될 것으로 전망된다. 업계에 따르면, 현재 푸꾸옥 내 위치한 숙박시설은 모두 700여 곳으로 객실 수는 2만4,000여 실에 이른다. 이 중 국제 표준의 4~5성급 호텔은 29곳으로 객실1만 3,470실을 갖추고 있다.

picked.t: “18km 갔는데 2,400원?” 그랩베트남 라이더, 12~13일 ‘앱끄기’ 단체행동 움직임 확산
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시에서 그랩바이크를 이용 중인 시민. 베트남 주요 차량호출 플랫폼 중 하나인 그랩(Grab) 소속 운전기사들 사이 오는 12~13일 이틀간 앱을 꺼두고 운행을 중단하자는 움직임이 확산하고 있다. 현재의 운임·수수료 체계와 실수령액이 차량 운행 비용을 제대로 반영하지 못한다는 게 이들의 주장이다. 최근 베트남 주요 사회관계망서비스(SNS)상에는 자신이 그랩 소속 파트너드라이버임을 밝히며 운행 거리와 기대에 못미치는 실수령액 등을 공유하며 플랫폼 측의 운임·수수료 산정 방식을 꼬집는 일부 누리꾼들의 게시물이 화제가 되고 있다. 이러한 게시물은 불과 며칠 사이 여러 플랫폼 운전기사들이 모인 커뮤니티에 퍼져나가며 사용자들에게도 실제 지불하는 요금과 기사들의 실수령액 간 차이에 대한 관심을 불러 모았다. 이 과정에서 일부 기사들은 소비자들이 지불하는 요금과 운행비 사이의 불균형을 보여주기 위해 자신의 운행 내역을 공유하기도 했는데, 한 그랩카(GrabCar, 자동차) 기사는 승객이 지불한 3만7,000동(1.4달러) 중 플랫폼 수수료 5,000동, 라이드커버(Ride Cover) 2,000동 등을 제하고 실제 손에 쥔 금액이 1만9,500동(75센트)에 불과했다는 내용을 올려 특히 많은 관심을 받았다. 승객이 지불한 요금 대비 실제 수령액은 52.7%에 불과했던 셈이다. 다만 업계 관계자는 차액 전부를 그랩이 가져가는 것은 명백한 오해라고 지적했다. 여기에는 플랫폼 수수료, 라이드커버 요금, 세금 등 여러 항목이 포함돼 있기 때문이다. 그랩에 따르면 라이드커버는 보험이나 특정 서비스를 보장하는 승객이 차량을 호출할 때 선택하는 추가 사항으로, 운전자 수입과는 무관하다. 일반 호출 서비스보다 저렴한 이륜차 호출 서비스인 그랩바이크띠엣끼엠(GrabBike Tiet Kiem)의 운임에도 불만이 제기됐다. 한 기사는 지난 5일 18.53㎞ 거리를 운행했지만, 실수령액은 4만6,900동(1.8달러)만 받았다며, 이는 ㎞당 약 2,530동에 해당한다고 자신의 운행 내역을 공유했다. 기사들은 이런 수입으로는 △연료비 △차량 정비 △감가상각비 △승객을 태우러 이동하는 시간 △기타 부대비용을 감당할 수 없다며 운임·수수료 체계 개편을 요구하고 있다. 온라인상에서 퍼지고 있는 이런 사례들은 일부 기사들의 개별 경우일 뿐, 플랫폼 전체 운영을 대표하지는 않는다. 다만 그럼에도 비슷한 사례 공유가 잇따르면서, 기사들 사이 앱을 끄고 운행을 중단하자는 집단행위에 대한 목소리가 힘을 얻게된 것이다. 그랩 측에 따르면, 현행 수수료 체계는 단순 고정 수수료율에 기반하지 않는다. 이륜차 파트너드라이버의 경우, 회사는 시간대·지역·수급 상황 등에 따라 달라질 수 있는 ‘유동 앱 이용료’를 적용하고 있어 흔히 거론되는 20% 또는 30%라는 수수료율은 건별 운임 배분 방식과 차이가 있다는 것이다. 또한 그랩은 운전기사와 함께 승객에게도 이륜차·자동차에 따라 건당 3,000~1만9,000동(12~73센트) 수준의 플랫폼 수수료를 부과하고 있다. 일부 기사들은 여러 수수료 항목 때문에 운행 전 실수령액을 가늠하기 어려운 반면, 운행에 들어가는 비용은 대부분 본인 부담으로 남는다며 요금 및 수수료 정책 변경을 요구하고 있다. 이 때문에 현재 그랩 기사들 사이에서는 오는 12~13일 운행 중단 동참을 촉구하는 움직임이 확산하고 있다. 이를 두고 일각에서는 그랩 파업에 대한 우려가 제기되고 있으나, 이를 주도하는 공식 단체나 주최자가 없는 만큼, 파업이나 집단행위로 보기는 어렵다는 의견도 존재한다. 운행 중단에 참여하는 인원도 불확실한 만큼, 실제 파급력에 대해서도 의문이 존재한다. 이 밖에도 시장에는 GSM이나 비(Be) 등 여러 차량호출 플랫폼이 활성화되어 있어 실제 소비자들이 겪을 불편도 제한적일 것으로 예상된다. 다만 이번 운행 중단을 지지하는 기사들 사이에서는 운행이 크게 줄면 그랩이 운임·수수료·소득 정책을 재검토하도록 압박할 수 있다는 의견이 힘을 얻고 있다. 이에 대해 그랩은 “최근 온라인상 기사들 사이의 이번 집단행동에 대한 내용을 인지하고 있다”고 원론적인 대답을 내놨다.

picked.t: What business leaders invest in to stay ahead
picked.body: More than 20 years after leaving university, Nguyen Xuan Hop, Global Procurement Director at Target, one of the largest retail groups in the U.S., returned to education to pursue a Master of Business Administration at British University Vietnam (BUV). For an experienced business leader who travels internationally, the decision required balancing nearly two years of study with professional responsibilities, family commitments, travel, tuition costs, and time away from work. It is a calculation shared by many mid-career professionals. According to NielsenIQ, while middle managers seek advancement into senior leadership, they also increasingly consider the return on investment (ROI) of postgraduate education. Foundation for long-term returns Postgraduate education is increasingly assessed not only by the qualification itself but also by the professional and financial value it can generate. Even amid economic uncertainty, multinational companies including Deloitte, PwC, and Unilever continue to fund master's degrees for selected employees to strengthen leadership, strategic thinking, and risk management capabilities. For individuals, the potential return extends beyond salary growth to include stronger management skills and professional networks. Financial return is one of the most measurable factors. The Financial Times includes "Value for Money" among its MBA ranking criteria, comparing graduates' earnings three years after completion with the cost of tuition and opportunity costs. Its 2026 data show that graduates from 100 MBA programs recorded salary increases of up to 200-250% within three years of graduation. Financial returns, however, are only part of the equation. As businesses become more complex, analytical thinking, leadership, and decision-making are increasingly important to career progression. The World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 identifies analytical thinking and leadership among key skills employers value. Graduate business programs can help professionals develop these capabilities through academic study and practical problem-solving. GMAC research in 2026 found that roughly two-thirds of global employers agreed that leaders in their organizations tend to hold graduate business degrees. Professional networks provide another potential return. Postgraduate programs bring together professionals from different industries and generations, allowing participants to exchange perspectives and build relationships beyond their existing circles. GMAC research involving more than 12,000 graduates from over 230 postgraduate programs found that relationships with classmates and industry professionals can contribute to career development. Together, these factors mean the value of postgraduate education can extend beyond the degree itself, combining knowledge, management capabilities, and professional relationships that remain relevant as business conditions change. Shortening the path to return on investment Once education is viewed as an investment, professionals must also consider how to maximize its value while managing time and financial commitments. This is reflected in the design of BUV's MSc International Business Management (MIBM) program. MIBM graduates receive dual degrees from BUV, ranked among Asia's top 43 MBA providers in the QS 2026 rankings, and Manchester Metropolitan University, whose Business School holds Triple Crown accreditation. For professionals seeking an international qualification, studying overseas can involve substantial tuition, living expenses, and time away from work and family. According to BUV, completing a master's degree in the U.K. can cost VND1.5 billion (US$57,180) to VND2 billion in total. BUV's MIBM, by comparison, is delivered in Vietnam over 12 months, allowing participants to continue their professional and personal commitments while studying. The program also connects students with business leaders and experts through BUV's network of more than 500 corporate partners. For Hop, practical application was an important part of the experience. "My time studying for an MBA at BUV fully met my expectations. It broadened my strategic perspective and allowed me to apply what I learned directly to my work at Target, from financial analysis and operational decision-making to business planning and supply chain optimization," he said. He also said interactions with professionals from different generations and industries helped him keep pace with developments in artificial intelligence and innovation while gaining broader perspectives on working in an increasingly international business environment. The MIBM program also includes international study opportunities and consulting projects in which students work on business challenges and apply academic knowledge in practice. picked.t: Southeast Asia’s richest man Pham Nhat Vuong surpasses Samsung, Alibaba billionaires in wealth
picked.body: Vuong, 58, chairman of Vietnam’s biggest listed company Vingroup, had a net worth of US$38.4 billion Tuesday afternoon, ranking 55th globally, according to real-time data by Forbes. His wealth has risen 35% so far this year, driven by the rally of Vingroup shares as the company deepened its investment in major property and high-speed rail projects. Shares of Vingroup have increased by 47% since the start of the year and are now hovering around its historic peak. The stock climb has boosted Vuong’s position up almost 40 places in the global billionaire ranking. In March this year, Forbes listed him as the 93rd richest in the world. Vuong is now richer than Jay Y. Lee, 58, the executive chairman of Samsung Electronics and the richest person in South Korea, whose fortunes were at $34.6 billion at the time of publishing, ranking 64th globally. Jay is the grandson of Samsung founder Lee Byung-chul and the son of longtime Samsung chairman Lee Kun-hee, making him the third generation of the founding family to lead the group. He joined Samsung in 1991 and gradually rose through its ranks, becoming vice chairman of Samsung Electronics in 2012 and effectively taking control after his father's illness and death in 2020. Similar to Vuong, whose wife and sister-in-law are also billionaires, Jay’s younger sisters Boo-jin and Seo-hyun and mother Hong Ra-hee are the second, third and fourth wealthiest in the country, respectively. Together, the family behind Samsung controls over $71 billion in fortunes. Vuong’s wealth also exceeds that of Chinese tech mogul Jack Ma, 61, whose wealth was at $26.3 billion at the time of publishing, ranking 95th in the world. Ma, a former English teacher, cofounded Alibaba Group Holding in 1999, helping build it into one of the world's largest e-commerce businesses. The once high-flying billionaire stepped down as Alibaba's executive chairman in 2019. After spending approximately a year overseas, Ma returned to China in 2023, just as Alibaba unveiled a plan to split itself into six businesses. Ma remains a mentor to the company and often encourages employees to innovate and adapt amid heightened market competition. Vuong, the founder of Vietnam’s first fully-fledged automaker VinFast, also surpassed Lei Jun, 56, the founder and CEO of tech giant Xiaomi, in wealth. Lei’s net worth stood at $21.7 billion at the time of publishing, making him the 127th richest in the world. Founded in 2010, Hong Kong-listed Xiaomi is now one of the world's most popular smartphone brands. In 2021, Lei announced plans to enter the electric vehicle market, describing the venture as his last major startup project. Xiaomi has since launched a series of pure electric and extended-range models, or hybrids equipped with gasoline-powered engines that can charge the batteries while driving. It delivered over 411,000 electric vehicles globally last year. In comparison, VinFast's figure for the same period was 196,900 units.

picked.t: Vietnamese, Russian leaders call for stronger trade cooperation
picked.body: At the meeting, which took place as part of General Secretary and President Lam's state visit to Russia, PM Mishustin noted his belief that the visit would create a turning point in bilateral cooperation in the time ahead. General Secretary and President Lam thanked Russian leaders, Government and people for their warm reception and conveyed PM Le Minh Hung's invitation to PM Mishustin to visit Vietnam at a convenient time. The top Vietnamese leader appreciated the role of the two Governments in concretizing and implementing agreements and orientations reached by the countries' high-ranking leaders, and called on the Governments to continue close coordination and make effective use of existing mechanisms, particularly the Vietnam-Russia Intergovernmental Committee on Economic-Trade and Scientific-Technological Cooperation. The two sides expressed delight at the progress made in bilateral relations across various areas of cooperation, including trade, investment, science and technology, education and training, people-to-people exchanges, and tourism cooperation. Notably, difficulties and obstacles previously raised by the leaders of the two sides have been addressed and improvements have been made in recent times. They also agreed to study the establishment of new cooperation mechanisms and specialized working groups in various fields, and pledged to encourage businesses from both countries to expand their operations in each other's markets, and promote business-to-business connectivity. General Secretary and President Lam called for stronger two-way investment towards a more balanced approach, saying following the success of TH Group, Vietnam encourages its businesses to invest in agriculture in Russia and Russian businesses to invest in industry in Vietnam. Emphasizing the importance of strengthening transport and logistics connectivity to expanding bilateral trade, PM Mishustin said the two sides should study solutions to improve the efficiency of maritime, rail and multimodal transport, thereby establishing stable supply chains and facilitating the exchange of goods between the two countries. General Secretary and President Lam highlighted the need for the two sides to establish new strategic connectivity through cooperation in transport, particularly railways, maritime transport and aviation. To enhance the effectiveness of economic and trade cooperation, he proposed the Russian government direct relevant ministries and agencies to continue reviewing and resolving difficulties and obstacles in economic, trade and investment ties; adopt appropriate solutions to issues related to tariffs, quotas, transport, logistics and market access; and increase Vietnam's commercial presence in Russia. Noting that Vietnam was the first country in the world to sign a free trade agreement with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), of which Russia is a member, the top Vietnamese leader also called on Russia to help encourage other EAEU member states to open their markets, remove trade barriers and eliminate the threshold-based trade remedy mechanism applied to Vietnamese goods. The two leaders spoke highly of the effectiveness of their oil and gas cooperation projects, considering them vivid examples of the efficiency of Vietnam-Russia cooperation. The Russia side expressed its desire to continue developing energy cooperation with Vietnam, not only in traditional areas but also in new fields in line with the needs and development orientations of both countries. General Secretary and President Lam and PM Mishustin shared the view that science and technology holds great potential to become a new driving force for bilateral relations, stressing the need to further elevate cooperation in this field. They also reached a consensus on the importance of studying the expansion of collaboration into areas such as new energy and biomedical technology, among others. The Vietnamese leader proposed making the most of Russia’s strengths in basic science, engineering and technology in conjunction with Vietnam’s needs for rapid and sustainable development. He also asked the Russian side to pay attention to supporting Vietnam in training high-quality human resources in fields where Russia has strengths and Vietnam has demand. The two sides agreed to promote cooperation in culture, tourism and people-to-people exchanges, thereby helping younger generations gain a deeper understanding of the history and traditions of the bilateral relations. The Russian PM expressed his belief that General Secretary and President Lam’s state visit to Russia and his talks with President Vladimir Putin will provide strong new impetus and identify important strategic orientations for bilateral relations in the new period. picked.t: Rapper joins handover of Hope Library in Vietnam's mountainous school
picked.body: Van Thuy Primary and Secondary School in Chien Thang Commune held the Hope Library handover ceremony on Aug. 21. The school previously had no dedicated reading room, with teachers and parents converting an old kitchen into a book storage area and setting up an outdoor reading corner under a corrugated-iron roof. Students lined the path to welcome guests, cheering as Den Vau arrived. The rapper joined reading and interaction activities and brought 100 books to contribute to the new library. A longtime book lover, Den Vau said he hoped books would open new paths for children, particularly those in highland areas. At the event, Den Vau recommended "Almanach of World Civilizations", which he first read in primary school. He encouraged students to read widely, study carefully and learn from their teachers. He also visited the library, joined organizers in decorating the space and asked students questions about books and characters. He later visited classrooms, handed out gifts, signed books and notebooks, and took photos with students and teachers. Den Vau has participated in various community and charity projects. In 2023, he donated all revenue from his music video to support highland children. Last September, he donated computer systems to two school points in Hung Yen and Quang Ninh, and in October contributed VND200 million (US$7,667) to support storm victims. He was among the top 10 recipients of the National Volunteer Award in 2023 and received the Golden Apricot Award in the Artist for the Community category that year. In March 2024, he was named one of the 10 Outstanding Young Vietnamese Faces by the Central Committee of the Ho Chi Minh Communist Youth Union. Den Vau, 37, whose real name is Nguyen Duc Cuong, is from Ha Long, Quang Ninh. Before becoming a singer, he worked as a garbage collector for seven years. He rose to prominence with songs including inspiring ones about family values and youth aspirations. The Hope Library was built in two months after construction began in May. The 60-square-meter facility was funded by contributions from VnExpress and FPT Online staff, with additional support from Hope Foundation, FPT Corporation and Vuihoc Company. The library has bookshelves, tables, chairs, fans and lighting, as well as a digital library with 15 tablets, headphones and Vuihoc online-learning accounts. The project continues the "VnExpress 25-Year Bookcase" program launched for the newspaper’s 25th anniversary and starts the "FPT 38-Year Library" project marking FPT’s 38th anniversary. The program aims to build or renovate 38 libraries nationwide, add at least 38,000 books, hold 38 workshops on AI, technology and digital skills, and equip all libraries with digital systems.

picked.t: Waist-deep water swamps Ho Chi Minh City streets at evening rush hour
picked.body: Heavy rain arriving right at rush hour left parts of eastern Ho Chi Minh City, including the former Districts 2 and Binh Thanh, deeply flooded. The underpass of An Phu intersection that leads to Ho Chi Minh City - Long Thanh - Dau Giay Expressway is flooded by half a meter. The intersection is the largest in HCMC. A tropical convergence zone has brought widespread rain to Ho Chi Minh City and southern provinces. Tran Van Hung, deputy director of the Southern Hydro-Meteorological Station, said that from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m. on Thursday, many parts of Ho Chi Minh City recorded more than 100 mm of rain, with Cat Lai receiving the highest total at 124 mm. "This is the heaviest rainfall since the beginning of the year," Hung said. A passing car created a large wave that caused 24-year-old Ha My’s motorbike to tip over in floodwaters at the intersection of Do Xuan Hop Street and Street No. 9. Another woman pushes her stalled motorbike through water on Do Xuan Hop. Drainage workers clear a manhole cover to ease flooding on Do Xuan Hop Street. On Quoc Huong Street in the former District 2, home to a large expat community, heavy rain left half a meter of water and stalled many vehicles. Hang carries her child on her back through about 500 meters of floodwater on Quoc Huong Street on the way home from school. A delivery driver pushes through a flooded stretch to complete a drop-off. An Indian family wades through Quoc Huong floodwaters to get home. On Chu Van An Street in Binh Thanh, Dat clears trash, including large plastic bags, to prevent storm drains from clogging. "Many households leave Styrofoam boxes and other waste in front of their homes, and it all accumulates on the street. I have to take the trouble to clear it away so the drains can function," he said. In an alley off Chu Van An, water rose to nearly a meter and poured into a row of homes. Many households propped metal sheets and boards against their doors but still could not keep the water out. Nguyen Van Ti uses a pump to draw water out of his living room. He said Chu Van An Street was widened in work completed late last year, but the heavy rain still left the alley where his family lives deeply flooded. "I thought that after the road was upgraded, the drainage system would help reduce flooding in the alleys, but today the water still came into the house. It's very inconvenient," he said. picked.t: 베트남-러시아 “포괄적 전략 동반자 관계, 한층 강화” 합의…양국 정상회담
picked.body: 또 럼 베트남 당서기장 겸 국가주석(왼쪽)과 블라디미르 푸틴 러시아 대통령이 정상회담 중인 모습. (사진=vna) 베트남과 러시아가 새로운 시대를 맞아 양국의 포괄적 전략 동반자 협력 관계를 한층 강화하기로 뜻을 모았다. 또 럼(To Lam) 베트남 공산당 서기장 겸 국가주석은 러시아를 국빈 방문 중이던 지난 9일 러시아 크렘린궁에서 블라디미르 푸틴 러시아 대통령과의 정상회담을 갖고 양국 협력 방안을 논의한 뒤 이러한 내용을 담은 공동성명을 발표했다. 공동성명문에 따르면, 양국은 국방·안보 협력을 전략적 기둥으로, 에너지·석유가스 협력을 전략적 돌파구로, 과학기술·혁신·인적자원을 주된 성장동력으로, 문화·민간교류를 양국 국민을 잇는 다리로 삼기로 합의했다. 또한 △정치·외교 △국방안보 △경제·무역 △연료·에너지 △교통 △산업·농업 △과학기술 △교육·훈련 △보건의료, △민간교류 등 구체적 협력분야도 함께 명시됐다. 국제협력 부문에서는 양국이 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 내 협력 강화 의지를 재확인했다. 러시아는 베트남의 2027년 APEC 개최 성공을 전폭 지지하기로 했고, 베트남은 러시아의 2035년 APEC 개최 제안을 환영·지지하기로 했다. 러시아는 아시아·태평양 지역 구조에서 아세안(ASEAN)의 중심적 역할을 지지한다는 방침을 확인했다. 이 밖에도 양국은 상호신뢰와 이해를 높이고 해양 관련 사안을 정기적으로 논의하며 공동 관심분야의 실질 협력을 촉진하기 위해, 베트남-러시아 양자 해양대화체 신설 가능성을 검토하기로 합의했다. 앞서 럼 당서기장은 푸틴 대통령의 초청에 따라 지난 7~9일 사흘간 러시아를 국빈 방문한 바 있다.

picked.t: Volcanic eruption disrupts Vietnamese travelers' journeys from Indonesia
picked.body: Anak Krakatau sent lava spewing into the sky and volcanic ash over Jakarta and Lampung Province, and remained active through the weekend. Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was the first to suspend flights on Sunday morning and did not resume operations until 12:30 a.m. Tuesday. The disruption affected nearly 3,000 flights and more than 340,000 passengers, according to Reuters . Thu Trang, a traveler from Hanoi, found herself caught in a frustrating loop between her hotel and Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after her Sept. 6 return flight was rescheduled. She says passengers boarded the aircraft early on Sept. 6, only for it to taxi back and sit idle on the tarmac for over an hour before crew members asked everyone to disembark. The airport temporarily opened at around noon, allowing passengers to leave while awaiting updates. Ground staff initially told her the flight had been pushed back to 9:00 a.m. on Sept. 7. The departure was subsequently delayed three more times, to 11:00 a.m., 3:00 p.m., and 9:00 p.m. Early the next day, the airport's website indicated operations had resumed. When she went to the terminal at 1:00 a.m., Trang was advised to wait until 3:30 a.m. But at 3:30a.m, airline staff were nowhere to be found. She checked a few hours later on Flightradar24 and was left stunned: it showed her flight had taken off at 7:00 a.m. and was en route to Hanoi. She had received no notification from either the airline or her booking platform. By 11:00 a.m. on Sept. 8, Trang was still stuck at Soekarno-Hatta without official word. Out of pocket by VND4 million (US$160) in extra expenses, the constant back-and-forth has taken a toll on her well-being while her work back home remains on hold. "I'm exhausted and just want to go home," she says, annoyed with the conflicting updates from officials. Another tourist, Duy Manh, managed to avoid being stranded in Jakarta by rerouting through a third country. Traveling with friends since Aug. 28, he was scheduled to fly from Surabaya to Jakarta on Sept. 6 and onward to Hanoi, and he had booked six months earlier for VND4 million. When flights out of Surabaya were grounded on Sept. 6, his international leg was pushed to Sept. 8, and his domestic transfer to Sept. 9. Lacking travel insurance and needing to return urgently for work, he abandoned his original itinerary to find a transit route through a third country. On Sept. 7, he spent VND8.5 million (US$340) on a ticket from Surabaya to Singapore. Reaching Changi Airport that afternoon, he managed to catch a connecting flight to Vietnam the following day. "Even though the ticket was expensive, I consider myself lucky to make it back," he says. Local volcanologists describe the eruption as an "anomalous event," noting that strong winds and dry conditions spread volcanic ash, rich in sulfur and silica, over vast areas, posing severe risks to aircraft engines. Indonesia reopened five airports past midnight on Tuesday following a two-day suspension of operations, according to BBC. However, Anak Krakatau erupted three more times on Tuesday morning, the volcano monitoring agency said. While the eruptions were smaller than the earlier ones, they could still disrupt flights depending on the height of the ash plume and wind direction. Airlines operating in the region also adjusted their schedules in response to the disruption.
